Hi Soojin / Ben,

Thanks for the quick intro call earlier. We started pulling together workload numbers so the team can recommend models and sizing. High-level context: our product ingests patient-facing instructions and produces both short summaries (~50-150 tokens) and longer Q&A answers (~500-2,000 tokens) depending on the flow.

Current rough traffic: average 9,000 sessions/day, peak concurrent users ~150, avg requests per session 2. Typical request payloads include a variable-length history (we expect 8k tokens most of the time but 20% of sessions reach ~12k; rare clinical notes push to ~24k). Latency target for interactive flows is 700ms p95 ideally, but 1.2s acceptable for the longer answers.

Can you recommend a short candidate list of model variants we should evaluate (long-context vs low-latency), and an initial token-volume estimate per day and peak-hour profile? Also any immediate constraints we should expect for Dedicated vs Hosted at this scale?

I'll loop in Sales Ops for procurement timing.

Thanks,
Ari

Hi Ari — great context, thanks. Below is a concise starting recommendation and a few clarifying asks so we can finalize a handoff package and sizing. I've attached a lightweight shortlist + token estimate workbook for your team to review.

Model shortlist (initial candidates and rationale):
- Redwood-13B-8k-q4 (recommended for mixed latency + quality): good balance for summarization and mid-length answers; low memory footprint if quantized, predictable cost profile.
- Mistral-XL-32k (recommended for long-context Q&A): use for flows that require 12–24k windows; expect higher cost/latency but better coherence across long notes.
- Llama3-7B-4k-q3 (fast-fallback): lower cost, lower latency for short summarization and routine prompts where context window is small.

Key tradeoffs:
- Use Mistral-XL-32k on requests that exceed ~8k tokens; otherwise prefer Redwood-13B to reduce cost.
- Expect per-request token consumption to vary: short summaries ~100–300 tokens output, Q&A 600–2,000 tokens output. Input tokens will depend on truncation strategy—our estimate workbook assumes 30–40% of total tokens are input.

Initial token-volume estimates (workbook attached):
- Daily token estimate (combined in/out): ~18M–24M tokens/day (range depends on output verbosity).
- Peak hour multiplier: plan for ~8–12% of daily traffic in peak hour; estimate peak-hour tokens ~1.6M–2.9M.

Questions / asks to finalize sizing:
1) Can you share a few redacted sample payloads (short, medium, long) so we can validate tokenization assumptions?
2) What is the true p95 latency SLO for the product paths (interactive chat vs background summary)?
3) Any compliance requirements for Private deployment (VPC/HSM) vs Hosted?

Next steps: we propose a short handoff workshop (30–45m) with engineering + CS this week to lock the shortlist and confirm procurement path. If that works I'll send a calendar invite and attach the shortlist + a token estimate CSV.

Attaching: model_shortlist_v1.xlsx, token_estimates.csv

Best,

Thanks for the detail, Ari — and good notes, Soojin. Adding a few operational sizing and performance notes from the runtime side to help with Dedicated vs Hosted decisioning:

Throughput & pool sizing (rough):
- Steady-state (expected average): 60–80 rps of small-medium requests -> a 1–2 GPU Dedicated pool (A100-80GB or equivalent) with batching and prefix caching should cover this with headroom.
- Peak-hour handling (burst): assume 150 concurrent users, estimate 200–240 rps peak for short requests; plan for an autoscale burst to 3–4 GPUs in Dedicated, or fallback to Hosted mixed route for headroom.

Latency considerations:
- Quantized 13B models (q4) can hit ~200–500ms per short response in optimized path; long answers on 32k models will be ~800ms–2s depending on output length and batching.

Operational levers to control cost and latency:
- Prefix/KV caching for templated instructions (we saw 25–40% token savings in similar customers).
- Route short queries to low-latency fallback model; route long-context queries to Mistral-XL-32k with a higher cost bucket.
- Set a max output token cap on interactive flows and post-process longer generations asynchronously when appropriate.

Procurement / SOW note: attached is a draft SOW (sow_draft_v0.2.pdf) with two commitment scenarios (Dedicated reserved 2xA100 vs Dedicated 4xpeak autoscale). Sales Ops — please advise on timeline constraints for the reserved capacity proposal.

Link: https://console.redwood.ai/docs/ops/onboarding-sizing (internal)

Ben
